paper_title: Context Consistency between Training and Testing in Simultaneous Machine   Translation
caption: Ablation studies between Consistency-Bi and Consistency-Uni on test set of IWSLT14 De-En task of wait-k policy.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the BLEU scores for three different consistency regularization methods—Consistency-CE, Consistency-Uni, and Consistency-Bi—across varying levels of average lagging (AL) on the IWSLT14 De-En test set, as part of an ablation study for the wait-k policy. The x-axis, labeled “Average Lagging (AL)”, spans from 0 to 8 with tick marks at integer intervals, indicating the number of lagging steps. The y-axis, labeled “BLEU”, ranges from 20 to 32, with tick marks at 2-unit intervals, representing the translation quality metric. The plot displays three lines: the “Consistency-CE” method is shown with a purple dashed line and circular markers, starting at a BLEU score of approximately 19.0 at AL=0 and rising to about 31.2 at AL=8. The “Consistency-Uni” method is depicted with a green solid line and square markers, beginning at a BLEU score of about 25.2 at AL=0 and increasing to approximately 31.9 at AL=8. The “Consistency-Bi” method is represented by a red solid line with star-shaped markers, starting at a BLEU score of roughly 26.0 at AL=0 and reaching a score of about 32.0 at AL=8. All three methods show an overall increasing trend in BLEU score as AL increases, with Consistency-Bi consistently achieving the highest scores and Consistency-CE the lowest across the entire range.
